title: Accessibility and ordinary replacement of many-object operads
statement: Use $\Delta_X^{\mathrm{op}}$ from [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and the operads of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability]. The functor $X\mapsto\Delta_X^{\mathrm{op}}$ from small spaces to generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads preserves filtered colimits. The inclusion of ordinary nonsymmetric infinity operads in generalized ones has a left adjoint $L_{\mathrm{gen}}$; for every small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operad $\mathcal M$, its unit induces natural equivalences $\operatorname{Alg}_{L_{\mathrm{gen}}\mathcal M}(\mathcal V)\simeq\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal V)$ for every monoidal infinity category $\mathcal V$. Consequently $q:X\mapsto L_{\mathrm{gen}}\Delta_X^{\mathrm{op}}$ is accessible. The space of colors $q(X)_{[1]}$ is naturally equivalent to $X\times X$; for each map of spaces $f:X\to Y$, the color map induced by $q(f)$ sends $(x,y)$ to $(f(x),f(y))$ under these equivalences.

source.place: Proposition 4.1.7; Corollary 3.2.14 (ordinary operadic replacement); Remark 4.3.2; Corollary 4.2.8 and Definition 4.3.3 (colors). No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Let $j\mapsto X_j$ be a small filtered coherent diagram of spaces, with colimit $X$. The inclusion $\mathcal S\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ preserves colimits: a functor from a space into an infinity category $T$ lands in its core, so its mapping space is $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S}(X,T^{\simeq})$, and the colimit universal property in spaces gives exactly the colimit universal property in $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$. The functor classifying $\Delta_{X_j}^{\mathrm{op}}$ has value $X_j^{n+1}$ at $[n]$ by [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. Apply [lem-coef-spaces-kappa-limit-filtered-colimit] with $\kappa=\aleph_0$ and the finite discrete simplicial set with $n+1$ vertices to the diagram constant in that finite variable. For every $n\geq0$ the comparison $\operatorname{colim}_jX_j^{n+1}\to X^{n+1}$ is an equivalence. These comparisons commute with every projection and diagonal, since their composites with each colimit leg do. The objectwise characterization of colimit diagrams in $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal V)$ in [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], applied with $K=N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$, $\mathcal V=\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ and the small filtered index (whose evaluated colimits exist in $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$, as just shown), therefore shows that the cocone of classifying functors is colimiting in $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Cat}_\infty)$, i.e. identifies the colimit of the classifying functors with $[n]\mapsto X^{n+1}$.

Apply the straightening equivalence $\operatorname{St}_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}:\operatorname{coCart}(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Cat}_\infty)$ of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], which sends a cocartesian fibration to its fiber functor, to the cocone of classifying functors from step 1. Being an equivalence, its inverse carries that colimiting cocone to a colimiting cocone $(\Delta_{X_j}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\Delta_X^{\mathrm{op}})_j$ in $\operatorname{coCart}(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$, and the total-category functor preserves small filtered colimits by [lem-coef-filtered-operadic-unstraightening]. Hence the underlying infinity category of $\Delta_X^{\mathrm{op}}$ is the colimit of the underlying categories of $\Delta_{X_j}^{\mathrm{op}}$. The operadic forgetful functor detects filtered colimits, again by [lem-coef-filtered-operadic-unstraightening], so this is a colimit of generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads. This proves the first assertion, including coherent diagrams whose indexing category is not an ordinary category.

Use [lem-coef-marked-operadic-model-structures] to take the identity Quillen adjunction from the generalized operadic model structure to the ordinary one. Its right derived functor sends an ordinary fibrant operad to the identical generalized operad; on mapping spaces between such objects the enrichments are the identical inert-preserving functor enrichment. Thus it is precisely the fully faithful inclusion of ordinary operads. By [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] its left derived functor exists and is left adjoint to this inclusion; call it $L_{\mathrm{gen}}$. All objects of the source model are cofibrant. Factor the map of a generalized operad $M$ to the terminal object in the ordinary operadic model as a trivial cofibration $j:M\to RM$ followed by a fibration. Then $RM$ represents $L_{\mathrm{gen}}M$, and $j$ represents the derived unit, by the replacement formula in the cited derived-adjunction statement.

Let $P$ be any ordinary nonsymmetric infinity operad. In the ordinary marked operadic model, $j:M\to RM$ from step 3 is a trivial cofibration and $P$ is fibrant. The enriched model axiom in [lem-coef-marked-operadic-model-structures] therefore makes $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(RM,P)\to\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(M,P)$ a categorical weak equivalence. Its two represented infinity categories are exactly $\operatorname{Alg}_{L_{\mathrm{gen}}M}(P)$ and $\operatorname{Alg}_M(P)$, with all transformations, by the Hom identification in that same node. This proves the full algebra-category assertion, rather than just its core. Taking $P=\mathcal V^\otimes$ works for any monoidal infinity category, since it is an ordinary nonsymmetric operad. The map is restriction along the unit, so precomposition in $M$ and postcomposition in $P$ give its naturality, including higher simplices. No presentability of $\mathcal V$ has been assumed.

A left adjoint preserves every colimit that exists: for a colimit $Z=\operatorname{colim}Z_j$ the adjunction identifies $\operatorname{Map}(L_{\mathrm{gen}}Z,P)$ with $\operatorname{Map}(Z,P)$, which is $\lim_j\operatorname{Map}(Z_j,P)\simeq\lim_j\operatorname{Map}(L_{\mathrm{gen}}Z_j,P)$, where each $P$ is viewed in generalized operads on the middle expression. This is the colimit universal property. Applying it to step 2 shows that $q:X\mapsto L_{\mathrm{gen}}\Delta_X^{\mathrm{op}}$ preserves filtered colimits. The spaces clause of [lem-coef-accessible-infinity-pullback] states that the infinity category $\mathcal S$ of small spaces is presentable. The base-category clause of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability] states that $\operatorname{Opd}^{\mathrm{ns}}_\infty$ is presentable. These give accessible source and target categories with the small filtered colimits in question. The accessible-functor clause of [lem-coef-accessible-infinity-pullback] applies: preservation of $\kappa$-filtered colimits for some regular $\kappa$ is exactly accessibility of the functor. Taking $\kappa=\aleph_0$ and using the preservation just proved therefore shows that $q$ is accessible. The homotopy-pullback and completeness clauses of that node are not needed here.

source.place: Proposition 4.1.7 and proof of Proposition 4.3.5, accessibility consequence

proof.text:
Fix a small space $X$. Choose a small fibrant simplicial groupoid $G$ with $N_{\mathrm{hc}}G\simeq X$ by [lem-coef-simplicial-groupoid-models]. Define a simplicial multicategory $O_G$ with colors $(a,b)$ and operation spaces
$$O_G((x_0,y_1),\ldots,(x_{n-1},y_n);(y_0,x_n))=\prod_{i=0}^{n}G(y_i,x_i).$$
Substitution composes the corresponding arrows of $G$, with identities for units, so its associativity and unit equations are those of $G$. All these operation spaces are Kan, including the nullary space $G(y_0,x_0)$. By [lem-coef-simplicial-operator-nerve], $O=N_{\mathrm{hc}}O_G^\otimes$ is an ordinary infinity operad and $M=N_{\mathrm{hc}}D(G)$ identifies with $\Delta_X^{\mathrm{op}}$. Define $\Phi:D(G)\to O_G^\otimes$ on a string $(z_0,\ldots,z_n)$ by the list $((z_0,z_1),\ldots,(z_{n-1},z_n))$. Over $\phi:[m]\to[n]$, a tuple $u_i:z_{\phi(i)}\to w_i$ maps to the operation for the $i$th output whose first factor is $u_{i-1}^{-1}$, last factor is $u_i$, and intervening factors are identity arrows. This also covers a zero-length block: its operation is $u_i u_{i-1}^{-1}$. For composable tuples $u$ over $\phi:[m]\to[n]$ and $v$ over $\psi:[k]\to[m]$, the composite tuple in $D(G)$ is $w_j=v_j u_{\psi(j)}$. In the $j$th substituted output block, its first factor is $u_{\psi(j-1)}^{-1}v_{j-1}^{-1}=w_{j-1}^{-1}$ and its last factor is $v_j u_{\psi(j)}=w_j$; every internal join contains $u_i^{-1}u_i=1$. A zero-length inner block contributes $u_i u_{i-1}^{-1}$ and the same successive cancellations give these endpoints; when the final block has length zero they combine to $w_jw_{j-1}^{-1}$. If $\psi(j-1)=\psi(j)$ this is $v_jv_{j-1}^{-1}$ directly. Thus substitution agrees with the formula for the composite in every block. For identity tuples all endpoint factors and inserted factors are identities, proving identity preservation as well. Over an inert base map, each output block has length one; its two factors are invertible arrows in $G$, together giving an invertible unary operation. The resulting arrow is the canonical inert lift followed by a vertical equivalence, hence is inert. For $m=0$ the output is the unique empty list. Hence it induces a generalized operad map $f:M\to O$.

We verify the hypotheses of [lem-coef-operadic-localization-operation-criterion] for $f$. The zero-fiber of $M$ is $X$, a space. The unary category of $O_G$ has Hom from $(a,b)$ to $(c,d)$ equal to $G(c,a)\times G(b,d)$, with the first factor composed in reverse order. It is $G^{\mathrm{op}}\times G$ and is a simplicial groupoid. The unary category of $D(G)$ is $G\times G$, and $f_{[1]}$ is inversion on the first factor and identity on the second. It is therefore an isomorphism of simplicial groupoids. The operator-nerve fiber formula in [lem-coef-simplicial-operator-nerve] and the coherent-nerve comparison of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] apply. The nerve preserves products directly: a simplicial functor from $\mathfrak C[\Delta^k]$ into a product is a pair of simplicial functors, compatibly with every simplicial operator. Inversion identifies $N_{\mathrm{hc}}G^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $N_{\mathrm{hc}}G$. Thus they give $O_{[1]}\simeq X\times X$, a space, and show $f_{[1]}$ is an equivalence. This identifies the color comparison before applying the approximation theorem; we have not presumed that replacement preserves colors in general.

Fix a color $(x,y)$ and compute the operation spaces in [lem-coef-operadic-localization-operation-criterion] arity by arity using the formulas of step 6 and [lem-coef-simplicial-operator-nerve]. For arity $n\geq1$, an $O$-operation consists of its input pairs, an arrow from $x$ to the first initial endpoint, arrows joining each adjacent pair of endpoints, and an arrow from the final endpoint to $y$. Source-change equivalences over the identity of $[n]$ vary those endpoints. Write $A_x$ for the groupoid of arrows starting at $x$ and $B_y$ for the groupoid of arrows ending at $y$, including all higher homotopies. The resulting arity-$n$ space is
$$A_x\times\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,X)^{n-1}\times B_y.$$
The corresponding $M$-operation has the same two endpoint factors and just one object at each of the $n-1$ intermediate positions, so its space is $A_x\times X^{n-1}\times B_y$. Inversion at the initial endpoint identifies the two endpoint conventions. The map induced by $f$ inserts the constant path at each internal position. Evaluation at an endpoint in $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,X)$ is inverse to constant paths up to the homotopy contracting $\Delta^1$ to that endpoint. Thus the displayed map is an equivalence, with its inverse given by evaluation on the intermediate joining arrows. The factors $A_x$ and $B_y$ are contractible, with identity arrows as initial or terminal objects; none of their homotopies is discarded. In arity zero an $M$-operation is a point $z$ with paths $z\to x$ and $z\to y$, modulo equivalences of $z$. Composition $b a^{-1}$ identifies its space with $\operatorname{Map}_X(x,y)$; the inverse sends a path $h:x\to y$ to $(z=x,a=1_x,b=h)$. These are inverse up to the source-change equivalence $a$, and agree with $f$. The nullary $O$-operation space is the same path space by its defining formula and [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Taking the disjoint union over arities proves the required equivalence of operation spaces. Crucially only source changes over identity arity maps have been used. Apply [lem-coef-operadic-localization-operation-criterion] to conclude that $f$ has the ordinary operadic replacement universal property. Since step 3 constructed that replacement, uniqueness of a representing object identifies $q(X)$ with $O$, compatibly with the unit. The color comparison in step 7 therefore proves $q(X)_{[1]}\simeq X\times X$.

source.place: Theorem 4.2.7, checked using corrected Corollary E.0.1 instead of uncorrected Corollary A.6.9

proof.text: Let $\eta_X:\Delta_X^{\mathrm{op}}\to q(X)$ be the unit of step 3. The equivalence $e_X:q(X)\to O$ of step 8 was induced by $f$, so $e_X\eta_X\simeq f$. Step 7 shows that $f_{[1]}$ is an equivalence; since $(e_X)_{[1]}$ is an equivalence too, the unit $(\eta_X)_{[1]}$ is an equivalence. By [def-coef-complete-algebroid] its source is naturally $X\times X$. Hence the desired natural color equivalence is the unit itself, $X\times X\xrightarrow{\sim}q(X)_{[1]}$. For any map $h:X\to Y$, naturality of the adjunction unit gives $q(h)_{[1]}(\eta_X)_{[1]}\simeq(\eta_Y)_{[1]}(h\times h)$. The unit is a coherent natural transformation, so these compatibilities include higher simplices. Under its inverse color identifications, the induced color map is exactly $(x,y)\mapsto(hx,hy)$. No choice of a functor between groupoid models is needed.

Nullary operations are checked separately; the item statement is unchanged.
